summary: All 72 current wrong-option messages insert malformed generated prompt text (for example, “The prompt asks to the test must construct requests ... which construction input should be explicit”), so they are not grammatical or usable causal explanations. Stable target IDs remain valid. The earlier v1 positive key/identity evidence is reused because v2 changed only constraints, feedback, and interactions; current keys retain each explicit construction-input meaning. i001 also has a plausible second answer: injecting a shared process-wide clock that tests reset meets the stated controlled-clock task absent a concurrency/isolation premise. The construction-input framing weighs against it, so this is recorded as a bounded ambiguity for author/reviewer resolution, not an independent identity change. I compared every shared/global alternative across the full unit rather than assuming shared state is invalid: most fail the stated request for an explicit constructor input, or the case’s fixed/controlled distinct values. The i001 option explicitly says “Inject a shared, process-wide clock,” so it remains a viable controlled constructor dependency for sequential before/after cases absent a concurrency or isolation requirement; that case has an unresolved second-answer risk.
